description_summary: 12-month unduplicated student headcounts broken down by enrollment level, sex, and race/ethnicity, covering both undergraduate and graduate students. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYLEV; the table contains total counts for men and women and counts for each of the nine race/ethnicity categories.

12-month instructional activity measured in total credit hours and/or contact hours, reported for undergraduate and graduate instruction and used to derive 12-month FTE enrollment. The record grain is institution and instructional level; unlike the headcount table, this table contains instructional workload measures rather than unduplicated student counts.

Awards and degrees conferred from July 1, 2004, through June 30, 2005, reported by 6-digit CIP program, award level, first or second major, race/ethnicity, and gender. The table covers eligible postsecondary institutions reporting completions, including certificates and degrees; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM (first or second major), and AWLEVEL. It contains total awards and sex-specific totals, plus totals and sex-specific counts for all nine race/ethnicity categories. Although the description also mentions a July 1, 2005–June 30, 2006 period, the table’s stated coverage is July 1, 2004–June 30, 2005.

Fall enrollment counts by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), attendance status, and student level (EFLEVEL), with total and male/female counts, including full- and part-time totals.

Fall enrollment counts by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), attendance status, and student level (EFALEVEL), with total and male/female counts for each race/ethnicity category and attendance status.

Fall enrollment counts by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), age category (EFBAGE), and student level (LSTUDY); age-based enrollment reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2005 (odd) has data, subject to the institution’s reporting.

First-time freshman counts by state of residence, including the number who graduated from high school the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and state of residence (EFCSTATE); residence reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2005 (odd) is an optional reporting year and data may be missing for institutions that did not report.

Institution-level total entering-class counts and first-year retention rates for institutions with undergraduate students. Entering-class data are available only for academic-year institutions; institutions offering short programs of less than one year do not have retention data. For 2005, the table contains retention rates but not the additional counts used to generate those rates; the retention measure follows students who began in fall 2005 into fall 2006.

Institutional finance amounts for public institutions using GASB 34/35, including revenues by source, expenditures by function and natural classification, and assets and liabilities. The row grain is one public institution identified by UNITID, excluding the separate component-unit records in the companion files.

Assets, liabilities, and net assets for FASB-reporting component units affiliated with public GASB institutions. Each row represents a named component unit associated with a primary institution, identified by the institution and component-unit entity name, and includes the component unit’s general nature; component-unit financial data are available for fiscal years 2001 through 2006, including 2005.

Assets, liabilities, and net assets for GASB-reporting component units affiliated with public GASB institutions. Each row represents a named component unit associated with a primary institution, identified by the institution and component-unit entity name, and includes the component unit’s general nature; component-unit financial data are available for fiscal years 2001 through 2006, including 2005.

Institutional finance amounts for all private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB, including revenues by source, expenditures by function and natural classification, and assets and liabilities. The row grain is one institution identified by UNITID; public institutions using GASB belong in the separate GASB institutional table.

Institutional finance amounts for private for-profit institutions using FASB, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities. The row grain is one private for-profit institution identified by UNITID.

Graduation and transfer outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohorts at four-year and two-year institutions, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Records are uniquely defined by IPEDS ID (UNITID), cohort and graduation status (GRTYPE); four-year records distinguish bachelor’s-degree-seeking students from students seeking other credentials and include bachelor’s completion milestones at 100%, 125%, and 150% of normal time, while two-year records cover completion or transfer within 150%.

Graduation and transfer outcomes for the 2002 cohort of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-2-year institutions. Institution/cohort records contain the number enrolled and the number completing a program or transferring within 150% of normal time; the cohort year is fixed at 2002.

Fall staff counts broken down by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, and faculty/tenure status. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPRECTP, which combines occupational category, tenure status, and full- or part-time status.

Fall payroll staff counts broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, gender, and full- or part-time status. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SABDTYPE, which defines the occupational and full-/part-time category; race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2005 (odd) has data under that rule.

Fall payroll employee counts broken down by primary function/occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender. This applies to degree-granting institutions with fewer than 15 full-time employees, all nondegree-granting institutions, and related administrative offices; each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SCNLEVEL, the primary-function/occupation category. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2005 (odd) has data under that rule.

Fall full-time instruction, research, and public-service staff counts broken down by faculty/tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender. This applies only to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices; each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK, combining faculty/tenure status and academic rank. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2005 (odd) has data under that rule.

New-hire counts broken down by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender; new hires are full-time permanent employees hired for the first time or after a break in service between July 1 and October 31 of the survey year. This applies only to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices; each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SGTYPE, the primary-occupation category. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2005 (odd) has data under that rule.

Full-time nonmedical instructional staff counts and salary outlays broken down by gender, academic rank, and contract length, including 9/10-month, 11/12-month, and equated 9/10-month contracts. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID, ARANK, and CONTRACT.
Counts of full-time nonmedical instructional staff with contracts shorter than nine months, broken down by academic rank. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK.

Full-time nonmedical instructional staff receiving fringe benefits, with total and average benefit expenditures, broken down by contract length and benefit-plan type. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and BENTYPE.

Institution-level response-status records with one set of indicators for each IPEDS survey component, including response, nonresponse with imputation, applicability, parent/child or multiple-campus reporting, and revised-submission status.

Institution directory records containing names, addresses, contact and web links, active and Title IV participation indicators, and institution-level control, level, highest award, and Carnegie classification variables. The grain is one record per institution.

Institution-level records of educational offerings, award levels, control and affiliations, special learning opportunities, services, and athletic associations, plus applicant, admission, and test-score variables. Admissions and test-score fields are restricted to institutions that do not have an open-admission policy.

Institution-level student-charge records for full academic-year programs at institutions primarily using semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or another academic calendar measured in credit hours. Variables cover undergraduate and graduate tuition and required fees for full- and part-time students, first-professional charges, and published price of attendance for full-time first-time undergraduates.

Institution-level student-charge records for vocational or occupational programs measured in clock hours or primarily in credit hours but reported by full program length. The record includes the number of programs, price of attendance for the largest program, and tuition and fees plus books and supplies for up to five additional programs.
Institution-level records containing the institution’s mission statement or the web address where it is available; one record per institution.

Student financial aid counts and average aid amounts for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, covering aid received from July 1, 2004, through June 30, 2005. The table is reported at the institution-by-aid-source-and-aid-type grain and includes federal grants, state or local grants, institutional grants, and student loans; it is restricted to the specified undergraduate population.
